speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are an adolescent presenting with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history of bone fragility. To begin our assessment, have you experienced multiple fractures from minor trauma, such as falling from standing height?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (specifically 17α-hydroxylase deficiency).

The combination of ambiguous genitalia at birth, delayed puberty, hypertension (implied by maternal hair growth and potential androgen excess/deficiency patterns), and severe osteoporosis/fractures is highly suggestive of this rare form of CAH. I need to confirm her blood pressure and check electrolytes to finalize the assessment.

REQUEST TEST: Serum_Electrolytes, Plasma_Renin, Plasma_Aldosterone, 17-Hydroxyprogesterone, 11-Deoxycorticosterone.
REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_X-Ray, Hand_Wrist_X-Ray.
